bounds.domain: One Android deployment, one saved key and one renewal at a time. At most two renewal requests on two days, three acknowledgement rounds per renewal, one sign-in attempt that starts meanwhile, one newer credential action (a sign-out or a sign-in that replaces the saved key), one deadline and one plugin close. Renewal answers are a code, a refusal (401, 403, 409) or no usable answer. Acknowledgement answers are confirmed, already complete, retryable, refused, or confirmed at Cloud with the answer lost.
bounds.assumptions: The host's credential intent fence orders a renewal's guarded save against any newer credential action: the save and the action never interleave. The store compares the saved key with the one the renewal presented in the same guarded step. A day is projected to the nextDay event and Cloud's acknowledgement deadline to the deadline event. The inline and background acknowledgement rounds are one bounded sequence.
bounds.limitations: Revocation requests are sent but their delivery is not modeled. The model ends at the first revocation of the replaced key: the stored duty to revoke it (written before the save, retried in this process and on later starts, ended by a 2xx or a 401 answer, never applied to a key that is still the saved one) and the host's savedKeyRenewed hook run in the JVM fixtures only. A confirmed key that was never saved can stay active at Cloud until it expires when its revocation is lost or the process dies between the confirmation and the save. Cloud retiring the predecessor when its successor is acknowledged, the expiry warning, the preference record, the hourly automatic check, a pending browser sign-in from an earlier process, other deployments and overlapping plugin instances are outside this model. The JVM fixtures run the exact renewal methods against synthetic slot, HTTPS and lifecycle ports, and the exact save through plugin-native-agent's ResidentCredentialStore; they do not run Android or contact Cloud.
